title: Partially canonical axes in large language model representations
abstract: arXiv:2611.26920v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) develop rich internal representations of language, but whether their individual coordinate axes carry meaning, or whether meaning is encoded only in directions in representation space, is still an open question. A common assumption is that individual axes in LLMs are arbitrary. We here challenge this view: across 12 LLMs from six model families, the native axes are reliably more aligned with other models' representations, with human brain responses to language, and with interpretable linguistic features than randomly rotated axes that preserve the same geometry. The native axes nonetheless fall well short of the best achievable alignment, so LLM coordinates are not fully arbitrary but also not fully canonical: they are partially canonical. translated_title: 大语言模型表征中的部分规范轴
translated_abstract: 大语言模型对语言发展出丰富的内部表征，但其各个坐标轴本身是否承载意义，还是意义仅编码在表征空间中的方向上，仍是一个悬而未决的问题。一个常见的假设是LLM中的单个轴是任意的。我们在此挑战这一观点：在来自六个模型家族的12个大语言模型中，与保持相同几何结构的随机旋转轴相比，原生轴能更可靠地与其他模型的表征、人类大脑对语言的响应以及可解释的语言特征对齐。然而，原生轴远未达到最佳可实现的对齐程度，因此LLM的坐标并非完全任意，但也不是完全规范的：它们是部分规范的。关于LLM如何表征语言的理论，必须既能解释它们所学习的群体几何结构，又能解释为什么单个单元获得了在模型间重复出现的响应特征模式。
tldr: 该研究挑战了“大语言模型表征坐标轴是任意的”这一常见假设，发现在12个LLM中原生轴比随机旋转轴更能与人类大脑语言响应和可解释语言特征对齐，揭示LLM表征轴是“部分规范的”——既非完全任意也非完全规范。
en_tdlr: Challenging the assumption that individual axes in LLM representations are arbitrary, this study shows that across 12 LLMs, native axes align better than randomly rotated ones with other models' representations, human brain responses, and interpretable linguistic features, revealing that LLM axes are "partially canonical" — neither fully arbitrary nor fully canonical.
